title: Cross-language compatibility shim, lockfile regeneration, and migration playbook
creator: Avery Lin
description: Consolidate coordinated dependency bumps across Python/JS/Go SDKs, introduce a lightweight compatibility shim to translate deprecated API surface at the client layer, regenerate lockfiles, and publish a migration playbook. Goal: reduce runtime regressions from mismatched transitive deps and remove last-mile API surprises for customers during minor SDK bumps. This ticket covers the engineering work to implement the shim, validate across the test matrix, and ship migration docs and deprecation notices.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim implemented in Python/JS/Go that translates legacy parameter names to the new surface and can be toggled to strict mode
All three SDKs pass the cross-language compatibility matrix in CI (Python 3.9/3.10/3.11, Node 16/18/20, Go 1.19/1.20)
Lockfiles regenerated and validated against canonical dependency tree with no known vulnerable transitive packages
Migration guide and changelog entries published; automated deprecation warnings emitted for 4 weeks before strict mode default toggles
No customer-facing regressions in canary cohort (10% traffic) for 7 days; telemetry shows no increase in 5xx or client-side errors
notes: 2026-02-20: Kickoff - agreed on shim approach instead of immediate API removal to reduce churn for downstream users.
2026-02-22: Decision - shim will live in the client transport layer and perform shallow translation (param rename, enum mapping, header normalization). Heavy payload transformations are out of scope.

2026-02-25: Trade-off - shim adds ~0.4ms median latency in microbenchmarks; acceptable because it avoids rollout failures for many customers. Plan: expose opt-in 'strict' config default=false in initial release.

2026-02-27: Dependency plan - bump Python transport stack (httpx 0.24 -> 0.25), upgrade JS transport (undici 5.x -> 6.0), and refresh Go module pins (replace loose transitive version of github.com/some/dep with v1.4.3). We'll regenerate lockfiles across packaging systems (poetry.lock, package-lock.json, go.sum).

2026-03-01: Benchmarks - after transport bump + small JSON encoding change in Python, median client-side end-to-end latency dropped 8% on our internal echo test; throughput improved 12% for batch size 16 workloads.
2026-03-03: CI - added cross-sdk compatibility test job that runs translation scenarios (old param names, mixed-casing headers) against a local compatibility harness.

2026-03-04: PRs - created draft PRs for each SDK with the shim and lockfile bumps. PRs include an integration test that exercises legacy-to-new translations and validates telemetry events for deprecation warnings.
2026-03-05: QA notes - recorded a flaky case where Go client returned nil pointer when both old and new enum fields present; fix applied to shim (prefer new field, log warning).
public_messaging: We will introduce a compatibility helper in SDKs to smooth the transition for deprecated parameters: during the transition window the SDK will accept legacy field names but emit a warning. Customers on pinned minor versions are unaffected. Full strict validation will be opt-in initially and scheduled to flip after a 4-week deprecation window once telemetry shows low usage of legacy fields.
migration_notes: Python: replace client.call(param_name='old_name') -> client.call(new_param='value') ; shim translates 'param_name' -> 'new_param' while strict=False.
JS: the Node SDK will continue to accept snake_case keys in objects; prefer camelCase going forward. Example migration snippet included in CHANGELOG.
Go: regenerate go.sum after 'go get' bump. If you vendor dependencies, run 'go mod vendor' and verify no semver downgrades in the tree.
Rollback plan: revert transport pin in each SDK repo and toggle shim to legacy-first mode; deploy rollback in canary then prod if regressions appear.
Testing notes: include a small compatibility harness in downstream customers' integration test to assert no deprecated-key warnings before flip.
Changelog snippet will include exact replacement map and timeline + code examples per language (to be published with the SDK release notes).
